# Progress Node/.NET differential fixture

The activity slice additionally seeds all eight stored kinds, own private posts and followed authors who are public/private/CHILD/deleted/purged/blocked in either direction/missing/unfollowed. Only MILESTONE, QUEST and STREAK are exposed; current privacy and follow status are checked again on each GET. Read snapshots stay unchanged. The 999 synthetic follow-capacity rows are deleted in bounded test-only batches before this slice so it directly exercises the intended authors. Node limits author/candidate queries before filtering; small pages may therefore end before older visible items, and this baseline behavior is retained for migration parity.

The social sequence compares visible and private profiles, follow/unfollow state, mutual-friend views, blocking, and pagination across hidden friend candidates. Freeze purchase cases compare insufficient-gem and full-capacity rejections and verify that neither writes a receipt or ledger. Quest claims cover invalid periods, unknown quests, incomplete quests, and confirm failures leave state unchanged. Monthly claims additionally compare an old completed month with upgradeChest=true: one badge and activity, no gem or ledger credit, and replay with the same or another request key. Invalid monthly period formats and missing monthly rows are rejected. Historical chest replay preserves the persisted 24-gem credit rather than recomputing catalog rewards; zero credit, wrong quest identity and missing ledger each fail closed, with snapshots of wallet, quests, ledgers and activity. Shop coverage compares catalog affordability at 0/19/20/49/50/99/100/150 gems; all five available item kinds, quantity purchases and replay, stale catalog/unknown/disabled items, invalid quantities, max-owned/freeze capacity, exact-price energy refill and insufficient funds. Boost coverage compares timer/XP windows, same-kind stacking, replay, expired and exact-end activation, invalid kinds and exhausted inventory. Domain rows and energy outbox events are compared after mutations.

`progress-parity-scenarios.json` is a synthetic, deterministic account/economy/shop/social/billing/family/referral/promo sequence plus signed lesson, practice and purge-ack event cases and all four signed Progress job routes. `generate-progress-parity.mjs` runs it against the unchanged Node Progress router with its strict test-only memory store and generates `progress-node-golden.json`. The .NET `ProgressNodeParityTests` replays all 573 steps through ASP.NET Core and compares every response field, selected persisted tables and relay envelopes. A final test-only raw seed models legacy achievement rows with missing/null `earnedAt`; `GET /v1/me` keeps Node ordering for those rows, and the 2024 year review counts only the valid 2024 entry. The latest additions check exact-price freeze purchase, same-key replay, insufficient gems and the 364/365-day capacity threshold, along with classroom-code Unicode rejection, year review around Honolulu midnight on January 1, 2026, the accepted year range (2019 rejected, 2020 accepted), malformed/unknown/stale league-result requests, deleted-profile league reads/writes, follow capacity at 1000 and deleted-target access after purge, plus streak repair with mismatched/expired days, the exact two-day continuing path, gem and item success/failure, item replay, invalid payment and deleted-profile denial. Entitlement reads compare an absent row, MAX without expiry, active CANCELED, near-expiry GRACE, HOLD, REVOKED, EXPIRED and exact-now expiry, and verify GET does not write rows. The billing slice checks refund replay/payload conflict/terminal-state protection, same-state ordering, equal/older timestamp rejection, JavaScript-compatible overflow-date normalization and malformed-date failure without state changes. Gift coverage checks recipient denial, replay without extension, a non-expiring MAX entitlement, and replacement at the exact expiry instant; rewarded-energy replay cannot grant twice. Rewarded-ad coverage also checks a successful event and replay from a free owner, cross-user event-ID conflict, exact-now premium expiry, the 20-impression cap, and Honolulu local-day rollover. Referral reads count only ACCEPTED, QUALIFIED and REWARDED rows at their corresponding levels while excluding ISSUED and EXPIRED rows. Invite redemption preserves an active MAX invitee and grants a seven-day trial when expiry equals now. Promo parity covers active-null and exact-now entitlements, item inventory clamping at 999, and repeated user redemptions when maxRedemptions is null. Simulation is enabled only in the parity test composition; production remains closed. Rollover covers Pacific/Honolulu and Pacific/Kiritimati just after UTC midnight, freeze protection, streak loss and repeated ticks. It also proves the 400-day catch-up boundary resumes on a later tick and a malformed stored learning day is reported for retry without changing the wallet. League settlement waits for a nonzero watermark before closing after zero and remains idempotent; a full ten-member cohort checks equal instants expressed with different UTC offsets, rank tie-breaks, tier movement and podium gem awards. A separate run confirms settlement rejects one millisecond before the Monday UTC cutoff and closes exactly at the boundary. Purge removes a private reward row plus 81 activity rows across transactions. Relay ACKs both entitlement targets, retries attempt 10 to a persisted DEAD state, dead-letters a receiver's explicit non-retryable response on its first attempt and compares 1.5-second/3-second retry backoff under the same deterministic jitter. Friend-quest opt-in, gift/nudge interactions, simulated subscription cancellation and family join include repeated requests with different operation keys. Family removal covers owner removal of a departed user. Purchase reads include foreign-owner rejection. Family code derivation uses the same explicit non-secret test value as Node's test kit; production still requires its own server-side secret.

From the repository root, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```powershell
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-progress-parity.mjs --check
```

Regenerate without `--check` only when intentionally updating the reviewed baseline or scenarios. Review the generated diff; do not manually edit or format the golden file. The fixture records hashes of the Node source tree and exact scenario bytes, so stale inputs are rejected in CI.

The only volatile values normalized are generated deletion/outbox event UUIDs and outbox row IDs. Equal-time outbox candidates and their delivery envelopes are sorted by canonical content because random event IDs do not define a cross-runtime delivery order. Receipt `responseJson` and outbox `payloadJson` are parsed for structural comparison, preserving their complete semantic content. Scenario trace IDs and operation keys are fixed. This proves the scripted local sequence, not all relay retry/backoff outcomes, concurrent Appwrite transactions, cloud permissions or Flutter acceptance. Neither production runtime invokes the other or uses these stores.

# Learning Node/.NET differential fixture

`learning-parity-scenarios.json` has 81 deterministic lifecycle steps. It enrolls a synthetic learner, reads published course/manifest/bundle/path plus the default energy view, checks JavaScript-compatible exponent notation for numeric `limit`, then syncs a complete offline log against signed `vi_en/v2` content. It verifies the same local completion replays under a new operation/key and a changed answer log conflicts. The sequence then starts/replays a lesson session, verifies an invalid grading answer does not prevent a valid retry, abandons/replays that LESSON session, resets and compares a stale-revision conflict, checks report receipt creation/replay/body-conflict, seeds review/mistake/activity rows and compares paged review/vocabulary/mistake/activity reads, starts and abandons a REVIEW session, compares all 12 session-start mode outcomes, then starts a STORIES session and removes the course while it is active. The final four steps compare `/health`, unauthenticated `/ready` (401), and signed `/internal/outbox-watermark`, including PENDING/LEASED/DEAD rows before the cutoff while excluding ACK and an event exactly on the cutoff. The activity rows are seeded only inside the test fixture because the current Node service has no activity progress writer. `generate-learning-parity.mjs` builds the test-only Node kit and writes `learning-node-golden.json`; `LearningNodeParityTests.EnrollmentLifecycleSessionAndAnswerSequenceMatchesNodeResponsesAndRows` replays the same requests through ASP.NET Core with fixed time, identity, signed content and an optimistic in-memory row driver. The fixture compares full responses plus enrollment, session, slot, answer, mistake, review, activity, report and relevant receipt rows. The generated event ID in the offline session result is normalized because each runtime creates it independently. It excludes only the Node test app's publication receipt because the .NET reader is supplied with that already-published content.

The same fixture also contains a 16-case completion differential, exercised by `LearningNodeParityTests.AuthoredModeCompletionsMatchNodeResponsesAndEffects`. It compares all 12 modes plus TEST_OUT/CHECKPOINT pass and fail, an assisted MASTERY completion, and a REVIEW wrong-first-attempt followed by a correct retry. Responses and session, enrollment, answers, review schedule, mistakes, outbox and receipts are compared. These cases use locally re-signed test bundles with server-authored mode configuration; no cloud content is changed. A separate four-step publication fixture checks publish, same-key replay, duplicate-version rejection and persisted rows; a two-step outbox fixture compares retry/backoff then acknowledgement, including the delivery report and stored row; a signed HTTP dispatch fixture compares the scheduler response, delivery report and acknowledged row; a one-step immediate relay fixture compares delivery ID and persisted retry state after commit.

From the repository root, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```powershell
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-learning-parity.mjs --check
```

Regenerate only for an intentional scenario or baseline change, then review the diff. The fixture hashes the Learning and Shared Node source and exact scenario bytes. It proves these deterministic local flows; durable Appwrite concurrency, Flutter acceptance and production key/config operations remain separate gates.

# AI routes Node/.NET differential fixture

`ai-parity-scenarios.json` replays 25 deterministic steps with speech disabled: capabilities, filtered conversation history, tutor fallback/replay, entitlement denial, disabled voice-provider behavior, missing and stored assessment reads, an entitled roleplay through four authored tutor turns and completion, monotonic heartbeat, stale-epoch rejection, repeated close, foreign-owner denials, and a valid assessment with null score plus receipt replay. The final route step compares owner rows for conversations, outbox, receipts, usage, voice sessions, active slots and assessment jobs against Node. The same fixture runs two dispatcher steps, retry/backoff then ACK, and compares each delivery report and persisted outbox row with Node. It compares the signed HTTP relay URL, body, HMAC headers, and six Node/.NET response outcome classifications, then exercises immediate-after-commit retry and compares the event ID and persisted row. `generate-ai-parity.mjs` runs these traces through the unchanged Node AI implementation and records `ai-node-golden.json`; `AiConversationTests.DisabledSpeechRouteSequence_MatchesNodeResponses` replays calls through ASP.NET Core and compares full status/body responses plus persisted rows. `AiConversationTests.Dispatcher_RetryThenAckMatchesNodeReportsAndPersistedRows` compares reports and rows after each dispatcher step, `AiConversationTests.HttpRelay_MatchesNodeSignedRequestAndOutcome` compares signed request bytes/headers and status mapping, and `AiConversationTests.ImmediateRelay_RetryMatchesNodeDeliveryAndPersistedRow` checks post-commit retry behavior. The fixture seeds a separate MAX test entitlement and active voice session, captures the deterministic conversation ID between requests, and verifies receipt replay. It checks Node AI and Shared source hashes plus exact scenario bytes.

`ai-speech-parity-scenario.json` exercises one provider-on Azure assessment with deterministic silence WAV, synthetic key, and canned Azure JSON returned by a fake fetch. `generate-ai-speech-parity.mjs` records the Node status/body for create, idempotent replay and GET at the exact 24-hour expiry boundary, the normalized Azure request, and persisted `a_jobs`, `a_receipts` and `a_usage` rows. `AiConversationTests.Assessment_AzureProviderOnSequenceMatchesNodeResponsesProviderRequestAndRows` repeats the fixture through ASP.NET Core with an advancing fake clock and fake `HttpMessageHandler`; no network call is made.

`ai-voice-turn-parity-scenario.json` covers the provider-on TURN flow: seeded MAX entitlement, session and conversation creation, one Azure-assessed authored turn, and idempotent replay. `ai-assessment-fallback-parity-scenario.json` and `ai-assessment-assembly-parity-scenario.json` cover Azure failure followed by canned Deepgram or AssemblyAI transcription. `ai-voice-turn-fallback-parity-scenario.json` and `ai-voice-turn-assembly-parity-scenario.json` cover the same fallback providers through a voice-turn route. Every fixture uses synthetic WAV and credentials, canned provider responses and injected fake HTTP; Node/.NET compare the response/replay sequence, normalized provider request(s), and persisted rows. No network call is made. Azure assessment/voice-turn primary flows and both assessment/voice-turn fallback flows have local parity. Real scorer quality, device privacy/cost, and durable Appwrite acceptance remain pending.

From the repository root, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```powershell
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-parity.mjs --check
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-speech-parity.mjs --check
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-voice-turn-parity.mjs --check
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-assessment-fallback-parity.mjs --check
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-assembly-fallback-parity.mjs --check
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-voice-turn-fallback-parity.mjs --check
node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-ai-voice-turn-assembly-parity.mjs --check
```

Regenerate only for an intentional scenario or baseline change, then review the diff.

## Quest chest creation

Quest chest creation has eight controlled-entropy Node/.NET cases covering every success/failure roll combination at the 63/64 boundary. Responses and all quest, wallet, ledger, activity and receipt rows match; replay under the same or a new key does not reroll. Production still uses cryptographic entropy through the public parameterless constructor. The Node generator substitutes only the quest-chest entropy import inside its isolated test bundle; the .NET test supplies an internal instance constructor delegate. Neither test uses a process-wide .NET random override. Run `node backend-dotnet/tools/generate-quest-chest-parity.mjs --check`; CI checks this fixture before running `QuestChestNodeParityTests.CreationAndReplayMatchNodeResponsesAndEveryDomainRow`.
